mainTopic: Who lets a woman eat תרומה, worrying about a possible pregnancy, and the child of an ארוסה
overview: This amud finishes a משנה about which relationships let a woman eat תרומה and which take that right away. A כהן's daughter loses תרומה while she carries a ישראל's child. A ישראל woman gains it once she bears a כהן's child, so the son can do more than his father. An עבד never counts as a woman's offspring. A ממזר does count, and so does even a grandson fit to be כהן גדול, who can stop his own grandmother from eating. The גמרא then asks why we do not worry that a woman might already be pregnant. רבה בר רב הונא answers that חכמים worried only about pregnancy within marriage. רב חסדא adds that for the first forty days a fetus is 'just water.' Finally, רב and שמואל argue about a child born to an ארוסה. רבא and אביי debate whether we assume the ארוס is the father, and a second version of their argument begins and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A pregnancy from a ישראל stops her; a miscarriage brings her back
steps.stepSummary: Finishing the earlier case of a ישראל with a כהן's daughter: once she is pregnant she cannot eat תרומה, but if the fetus is lost she may eat again.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he got her pregnant, she may not eat תרומה. If the fetus was lost inside her, she may eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes a case it started just before: a כהן's daughter who had relations with a ישראל. Her pregnancy stops her from eating תרומה, and a miscarriage brings her right back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Relations alone with this ישראל did not stop her, but carrying his child does, because the fetus counts as a ישראל offspring. Once the fetus is gone, nothing is left to stop her, so she eats again.

keyTerms.meaning: he made her pregnant / she became pregnant
the holy portion of produce given to a כהן, which only a כהן and his household may eat
the fetus was cut off, meaning a miscarriage

phrases.english: If he impregnated her, she may not eat terumah.
phrases.notes: The 'he' is the ישראל from the case right before this in the משנה, who had relations with a כהן's daughter.

phrases.english: If the fetus was cut off in her womb, she may eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: עִיבְּרָה — לֹא תֹּאכַל בִּתְרוּמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a משנה case that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A fetus from a ישראל stops a כהן's daughter from eating תרומה; a miscarriage removes the block.

steps.title: A כהן with a ישראל woman: only the born child lets her eat
steps.stepSummary: A ישראל woman who had relations with a כהן does not eat תרומה, even while pregnant. Once the child is born, she eats.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a כהן had relations with a ישראל woman, she may not eat תרומה. If he got her pregnant, she still may not eat. If she gave birth, she may eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה flips the case: now the man is a כהן and the woman is a ישראל. Neither the relations nor the pregnancy lets her eat, but the birth of the child does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since there was no marriage, the כהן does not make her part of his household. An unborn fetus cannot give her the right to eat. A born child who is a כהן can, and that is the new point here.

keyTerms.meaning: a ישראל woman, not from a כהן family

phrases.aramaic: הָיָה כֹּהֵן שֶׁבָּא עַל בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל —
phrases.english: If it was a kohen who had relations with an Israelite woman,
she may not eat terumah.
If he impregnated her, she may not eat.
If she gave birth, she may eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיָה כֹּהֵן שֶׁבָּא עַל בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The mirror image of step 1: the man is now a כהן and the woman a ישראל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A fetus does not let its mother eat תרומה, but a born כהן child does.

steps.title: The son is stronger than the father
steps.stepSummary: The משנה sums up step 2: the son can give his mother a right that his father could not.
steps.simpleTranslation: So it turns out that the power of the son is greater than that of the father.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה draws a short lesson from the case it just taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן father did not let the woman eat תרומה, but the son born to them does. So in this situation the child has more power than the father.

keyTerms.meaning: it turns out / so we find

steps.whatToRemember: A born child who is a כהן can let his mother eat תרומה even when his father could not.

phrases.english: It turns out that the power of the son
is greater than that of the father.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִמְצָא כֹּחוֹ שֶׁל בֵּן גָּדוֹל מִשֶּׁל אָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the lesson of step 2.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Here the son lets his mother eat תרומה, while the father could not.

steps.title: An עבד disqualifies through relations, not as offspring
steps.stepSummary: A new rule: an עבד stops a woman from eating תרומה by having relations with her, but never by being her descendant.
steps.simpleTranslation: A slave disqualifies a woman because of relations, but he does not disqualify because of being offspring.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens a new rule about an עבד. The next steps will explain it with an example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to stop a woman from eating תרומה: by ביאה, meaning relations, or by being her זרע, meaning offspring. An עבד works only the first way. He is never counted as her offspring.

keyTerms.meaning: disqualifies, takes away her right to eat תרומה

phrases.english: A slave disqualifies because of relations,
and he does not disqualify because of offspring.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָעֶבֶד פּוֹסֵל מִשּׁוּם בִּיאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new rule in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עבד disqualifies by relations but not as offspring.

steps.title: Building the case of a grandson who is an עבד
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks 'how so?' and sets up a family in which the grandson is an עבד.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? A ישראל woman married to a כהן, or a כהן's daughter married to a ישראל, had a son. The son had relations with a שפחה and she bore him a son. That son is an עבד.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks 'how so?' and builds a family tree step by step. It is setting up the result in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The grandmother had a son, and that son had a child with a שפחה. A child of a שפחה follows his mother's status, so he is an עבד and does not count as his father's offspring.

keyTerms.meaning: how so?, meaning 'how does this work?'
pressed himself onto, a polite way of saying he had relations

phrases.english: How so?
An Israelite woman married to a kohen,
or a kohen's daughter married to an Israelite,
and she bore him a son,
and the son went and pressed himself onto a maidservant,
phrases.notes: 'Pressed himself onto' is a polite way of saying he had relations with her.

phrases.aramaic: וְיָלְדָה הֵימֶנּוּ בֵּן — הֲרֵי זֶה עֶבֶד.
phrases.english: and she bore him a son — this one is a slave.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיצַד? בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְכֹהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an example of the rule in step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A family in which the grandson is an עבד, born to the grandmother's son and a שפחה.

steps.title: The grandson who is an עבד counts as no offspring
steps.stepSummary: Because the grandson who is an עבד is not counted as offspring, the grandmother is treated as if she had no descendants.
steps.simpleTranslation: If his father's mother was a ישראל woman married to a כהן, she may not eat תרומה. If she was a כהן's daughter married to a ישראל, she may eat תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the result for the grandmother after her husband and son have died. In both versions of the case, the grandson who is an עבד counts for nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ישראל widow of a כהן needs offspring from him to keep eating, and an עבד grandson does not count, so she stops. A כהן's daughter widowed from a ישראל may return only if she has no offspring from him, and since the עבד does not count, she returns and eats.

keyTerms.meaning: his father's mother, his grandmother on his father's side

steps.confusionAlert: The same grandson leads to opposite results. That is not a contradiction: in both cases he simply counts as no offspring at all.
steps.whatToRemember: An עבד is never counted as anyone's זרע, so he neither keeps a woman eating nor stops her from returning.

phrases.aramaic: הָיְתָה אֵם אָבִיו בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְכֹהֵן —
phrases.english: If his father's mother was an Israelite woman married to a kohen,
she may not eat terumah.
If she was a kohen's daughter married to an Israelite,
she may eat terumah.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיְתָה אֵם אָבִיו בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְכֹהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the result of the family set up in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A grandson who is an עבד does not count as offspring for the grandmother's תרומה rights.

steps.title: A ממזר both disqualifies and lets her eat
steps.stepSummary: A new rule: a ממזר counts as offspring, so he can stop a woman from eating תרומה and can also let her eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ממזר disqualifies and enables to eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens a new rule about a ממזר. The example comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike an עבד, a ממזר is a Jew and counts fully as offspring. So he affects the grandmother either way, depending on whom she married.

keyTerms.meaning: a child born from a forbidden union

phrases.english: A mamzer disqualifies and enables to eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַמְזֵר פּוֹסֵל וּמַאֲכִיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new rule set up as a contrast to the עבד rule in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ממזר counts as offspring for the תרומה rules, in both directions.

steps.title: Building the case of a grandson who is a ממזר
steps.stepSummary: The משנה sets up a family in which a granddaughter's son, born from a slave or a non-Jew, is a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? A ישראל woman married to a כהן, or a כהן's daughter married to a ישראל, had a daughter. The daughter married an עבד or a non-Jew and had a son. That son is a ממזר.
steps.whatsHappening: Again the משנה asks 'how so?' and builds a family tree. It is setting up the result in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the line goes through a daughter. Her son follows her and is Jewish, but he is a ממזר, so he still counts as the grandmother's offspring.

phrases.english: How so?
An Israelite woman married to a kohen,
or a kohen's daughter married to an Israelite,
and she bore him a daughter,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָלְכָה הַבַּת וְנִישֵּׂאת לְעֶבֶד אוֹ לְגוֹי
phrases.english: and the daughter went and married a slave or a gentile

phrases.aramaic: וְיָלְדָה הֵימֶנּוּ בֵּן — הֲרֵי זֶה מַמְזֵר.
phrases.english: and bore him a son — this one is a mamzer.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיצַד? בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְכֹהֵן, וּבַת כֹּהֵן לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an example of the rule in step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A family in which the grandson is a ממזר, born to the grandmother's daughter from an עבד or a non-Jew.

steps.title: The grandson who is a ממזר counts as real offspring
steps.stepSummary: Because the ממזר counts as offspring, he keeps the ישראל widow of a כהן eating and stops the כהן's daughter from returning.
steps.simpleTranslation: If his mother's mother was a ישראל woman married to a כהן, she may eat תרומה. If she was a כהן's daughter married to a ישראל, she may not eat תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the grandmother's result, and it is the exact opposite of the עבד case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ממזר is real offspring of the grandmother's husband. If that husband was a כהן, she keeps eating through him. If that husband was a ישראל, his existence stops her from going back to her father's house.

keyTerms.meaning: his mother's mother, his grandmother on his mother's side

steps.whatToRemember: A ממזר counts as זרע. An עבד does not. That is why their results are opposite.

phrases.aramaic: הָיְתָה אֵם אִמּוֹ בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְכֹהֵן —
phrases.english: If his mother's mother was an Israelite woman married to a kohen,
she may eat terumah.
If she was a kohen's daughter married to an Israelite,
she may not eat terumah.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיְתָה אֵם אִמּוֹ בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְכֹהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the result of the family in step 8, the reverse of step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A grandson who is a ממזר counts as offspring, keeping one grandmother eating and stopping the other.

steps.title: Even a כהן גדול can sometimes disqualify
steps.stepSummary: A surprising new rule: even a grandson fit to be כהן גדול can sometimes take away a woman's right to eat תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A כהן גדול, sometimes he disqualifies.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה announces a surprising rule about a כהן גדול. The example comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You would expect the holiest כהן to only help a woman eat תרומה. The משנה signals that, as offspring, even he can block someone.

phrases.english: A High Priest, sometimes he disqualifies.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל, פְּעָמִים שֶׁהוּא פּוֹסֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new rule in the same pattern as the עבד and ממזר rules.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a כהן גדול can stop a woman from eating תרומה because he is her offspring.

steps.title: Building the case of a grandson fit to be כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: A כהן's daughter married a ישראל and had a daughter, who married a כהן and had a son fit to serve as כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? A כהן's daughter married to a ישראל had a daughter. The daughter married a כהן and had a son. This son is fit to be a כהן גדול, standing and serving on the altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks 'how so?' and builds the family tree. It is setting up the result in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The grandson's father is a כהן, so he is a complete כהן, fit even to be כהן גדול. But through his mother he is also the offspring of his grandmother's ישראל husband.

phrases.english: How so?
A kohen's daughter married to an Israelite
and she bore him a daughter,
and the daughter went and married a kohen,
and bore him a son —

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זֶה רָאוּי לִהְיוֹת כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל
phrases.english: this one is fit to be a High Priest
standing and serving upon the altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיצַד? בַּת כֹּהֵן לְיִשְׂרָאֵל וְיָלְדָה הֵימֶנּוּ בַּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an example of the rule in step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A grandson fit to be כהן גדול who is also the offspring of a כהן's daughter and her ישראל husband.

steps.title: He lets his mother eat but blocks his grandmother
steps.stepSummary: The same grandson lets his mother eat תרומה and stops his mother's mother from eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: He enables his mother to eat, and he disqualifies his mother's mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the result: one person, two opposite effects within the same family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His mother is married to a כהן, and he is a כהן child, so she can eat through him. For his grandmother, he is offspring from her ישראל husband, so she cannot go back to eating תרומה in her father's house.

keyTerms.meaning: he lets his mother eat תרומה

phrases.english: He enables his mother to eat,
and he disqualifies his mother's mother.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאֲכִיל אֶת אִמּוֹ, וּפוֹסֵל אֵם אִמּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the result of the family in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The grandson who is a כהן feeds his mother but blocks his grandmother, because he is her offspring from a ישראל.

steps.title: The grandmother's complaint
steps.stepSummary: The grandmother can say: let there not be many like my grandson the כהן גדול, since he keeps me from תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one says: 'May there not be many like my grandson the כהן גדול, for he disqualifies me from תרומה!'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with the grandmother's sharp remark, which drives home how strange this outcome is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her grandson brings the family great honor, yet he is the very reason she loses her right to תרומה. The line shows that the rule about offspring applies no matter how important the child is.

keyTerms.meaning: like my son, here meaning her grandson

steps.whatToRemember: Being offspring is what counts. Even a כהן גדול grandson blocks his grandmother if he descends from her ישראל husband.
steps.whyThisMatters: It completes the משנה's pattern: an עבד does not count as offspring, a ממזר does, and so does even a כהן גדול.

phrases.english: This one says:
"May there not be [many] like my son the High Priest,
phrases.notes: 'My son' here means her daughter's son, her grandson.

phrases.english: for he disqualifies me from terumah!"

steps.triggerLanguage: זֹאת אוֹמֶרֶת: לֹא כִּבְנִי כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the כהן גדול case with the grandmother's reaction.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Offspring status, not prestige, decides the grandmother's right to תרומה.

steps.title: The משנה already taught a known ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the משנה already contains the rule of a ברייתא: the wives of a שוטה or קטן who died are free from חליצה and יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: We already learned this, which the Rabbis taught: An imbecile and a minor who married women and died, their wives are exempt from חליצה and from יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by pointing out that the משנה already teaches the same idea as a ברייתא about a שוטה and a קטן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that a שוטה or a קטן cannot make a real marriage. So when they die, their wives are not tied to a brother at all, and need neither חליצה nor יבום. The גמרא is simply linking this known teaching to what the משנה says.

keyTerms.meaning: A person without sound mind, who cannot make a legal marriage
The ceremony that releases a widow from her husband's brother
Levirate marriage: the brother marries the childless widow

phrases.english: GEMARA:
We already learned this, which the Rabbis taught:
An imbecile and a minor who married women,
and they died, their wives —
phrases.notes: It's the husbands who died, not the wives.

phrases.english: are exempt from חליצה and from יבום.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנֵינָא לְהָא דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא on the משנה, after the earlier discussion of the grandson כהן גדול.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A marriage by a שוטה or קטן is not valid, so their widows need neither חליצה nor יבום, as the משנה already implies.

steps.title: The משנה's case: a בת כהן with a ישראל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: a בת כהן who had relations with a ישראל may still eat תרומה, but if she became pregnant she may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? If a ישראל had relations with a כהן's daughter, she may eat תרומה. If he made her pregnant, she may not eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה to set up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just having relations with a ישראל does not stop a בת כהן from eating תרומה. Pregnancy changes things: the unborn child of a ישראל father takes away her right to eat.

keyTerms.meaning: The holy portion of produce given to כהנים

phrases.english: How so?

phrases.aramaic: הָיָה יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁבָּא עַל בַּת כֹּהֵן —
phrases.english: If an Israelite had relations with the daughter of a כהן —
she may eat תרומה,
if he made her pregnant — she may not eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיצַד? הָיָה יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁבָּא עַל בַּת כֹּהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בת כהן who had relations with a ישראל still eats תרומה unless she became pregnant.

steps.title: Why not worry that she might be pregnant?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if pregnancy stops her from eating, we should worry right away that she may be pregnant, just as we separate couples for three months elsewhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since if he made her pregnant she may not eat, let us worry that maybe he did! Didn't we learn in a משנה: we separate them for three months, in case they are pregnant?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the משנה lets her keep eating, when we could worry that she is already pregnant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Elsewhere, after the swapped-wives case, the משנה separates the couples for three months because of a possible pregnancy from a single time. So here too, after one time, we should treat her as possibly pregnant and stop her from eating תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: Didn't we learn in a משנה?

phrases.english: Since if he made her pregnant she may not eat,
let us worry that maybe he made her pregnant!
Didn't we learn in a משנה:
We separate them for three months,
phrases.notes: This is the case of two couples whose wives got switched at the wedding (דף ל״ג ע״ב).

phrases.english: in case they are pregnant?

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּעִיבְּרָה לֹא תֹּאכַל? לֵיחוּשׁ שֶׁמָּא עִיבְּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling just quoted from the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that she may eat תרומה until she is known to be pregnant.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another משנה worries about pregnancy after one act and separates couples for three months; so here too we should worry and forbid תרומה.

steps.title: First answer: the worry is for lineage, not תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא answers that חכמים worried about possible pregnancy for lineage, but not for תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא said: About lineage they were concerned; about תרומה they were not concerned.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר רב הונא explains the difference between the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the swapped-wives case, the worry is that a child's lineage will be unclear, which is very serious. Here the only issue is eating תרומה, and for that חכמים did not worry about a possible pregnancy.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives the answers here

phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna said:
About lineage they were concerned,
about תרומה they were not concerned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא: לְיוּחֲסִין חָשְׁשׁוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by splitting lineage from תרומה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the topics: lineage versus תרומה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A possible pregnancy should be worried about in every area of law.
steps.terutzMaskana: The worry about pregnancy applies only to lineage, not to תרומה.

steps.title: But חכמים do worry about תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the first answer with a ברייתא: a get given 'one hour before my death' forbids the wife from eating תרומה right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: And about תרומה were they not concerned? But it was taught: 'Here is your גט one hour before my death' — she is forbidden to eat תרומה immediately!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבה בר רב הונא's answer by showing a case where חכמים do worry about תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this ברייתא, any hour might turn out to be the hour before he dies, so she might already be divorced. Because of that doubt she must stop eating תרומה at once. That shows חכמים are careful about תרומה too.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: And about תרומה they were not concerned?
But it was taught in a ברייתא:
"Here is your get
one hour before my death" —
phrases.notes: This is a ישראל woman married to a כהן; once divorced, she loses תרומה.

phrases.english: she is forbidden to eat תרומה immediately!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִתְרוּמָה לֹא חָשְׁשׁוּ? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה בר רב הונא's claim that חכמים did not worry about תרומה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא forbids תרומה immediately because of a mere doubt that the husband may die within the hour, proving חכמים do worry about תרומה.

steps.title: Second answer: worry in marriage, not in זנות
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא gives a new answer: חכמים worried about pregnancy from marriage relations, but not from זנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבה בר רב הונא said: About marriage they were concerned; about licentious relations they were not concerned.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר רב הונא drops his first answer and gives a new difference between the cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new split is not about the topic (lineage or תרומה) but about the kind of relationship. The swapped-wives case was within marriage, so pregnancy is a real worry. Our משנה is about זנות, where pregnancy is less likely (the usual explanation is that the woman tries to avoid it), so we do not worry.
steps.whatToRemember: She may keep eating תרומה because חכמים worried about a possible pregnancy only within marriage, not after זנות.
steps.confusionAlert: The final answer does not say חכמים ignore תרומה. The difference is marriage versus זנות, not lineage versus תרומה.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rather, Rabba bar Rav Huna said:
About marriage they were concerned,
about licentious relations they were not concerned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא: בְּנִישּׂוּאִין חָשְׁשׁוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 17 after the challenge in step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by type of relationship: marriage versus זנות.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The difference is lineage versus תרומה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The worry about pregnancy applies to relations within marriage, not to זנות, so the בת כהן keeps eating תרומה.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows no worry about pregnancy even after marriage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that חכמים worried about pregnancy from marriage relations. A ברייתא says a widowed בת כהן may immerse and eat תרומה that same evening.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did they really worry in a case of marriage? But a ברייתא teaches: a בת כהן who married a ישראל, and he died, immerses and eats תרומה in the evening!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבה בר רב הונא's answer from step 19, which said חכמים do worry about pregnancy from marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here is a married woman whose husband died. If חכמים worried she might be pregnant from him, she should not be allowed to eat תרומה. Yet the ברייתא lets her eat that very evening, so it seems there is no worry even in marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: In the evening, after the immersion takes effect

phrases.english: And in a case of marriage, were they concerned?
phrases.notes: This questions the answer from step 19, that חכמים worried about pregnancy only from marriage.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: a daughter of a כהן who married a ישראל,
and he died, she immerses,
and she eats תרומה in the evening!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְנִישּׂוּאִין מִי חָשְׁשׁוּ? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה בר רב הונא's claim that חכמים worried about pregnancy from marriage relations.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא lets a widowed married woman eat תרומה right away, showing no worry about pregnancy even in marriage.

steps.title: She may eat only during the first forty days
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that she may eat תרומה only for forty days, because a fetus under forty days is considered just water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: She immerses and eats until forty days. If she is not pregnant, then she is not pregnant. And if she is pregnant, until forty days it is just water.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the challenge by limiting the ברייתא: it allows her to eat only for the first forty days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Either way she may eat during those forty days. If she is not pregnant there is no problem, and if she is pregnant the fetus does not yet count as a child. So the ברייתא does not prove that חכמים ignore the worry of pregnancy in marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: Merely water; a fetus under forty days is not yet considered a child

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule that a fetus under forty days is 'just water' is an important principle that shows up in many places in הלכה.

phrases.english: רב חסדא said:
She immerses and eats until forty days,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי לָא מִיעַבְּרָא — הָא לָא מִיעַבְּרָא,
phrases.english: because if she is not pregnant, then she is not pregnant,
and if she is pregnant, until forty days
it is merely water.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: טוֹבֶלֶת וְאוֹכֶלֶת עַד אַרְבָּעִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא in step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the ברייתא to a time window (the first forty days).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to allow her to eat with no limit, which would mean there is no worry about pregnancy.
steps.terutzMaskana: She may eat only for forty days, when a possible pregnancy makes no difference anyway.

steps.title: אביי challenges with the end of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: אביי points to the end of the ברייתא: once the pregnancy is noticeable, she is 'ruined retroactively,' which seems to go all the way back.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: If so, say the end of the ברייתא: if her fetus became noticeable in her womb, she is ruined retroactively.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי questions רב חסדא's answer using the last part of the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Ruined retroactively' sounds like all the תרומה she ate since the husband died becomes forbidden, even in the first forty days. That would contradict רב חסדא's idea that the first forty days are fine.

keyTerms.meaning: Say the end part of the source

phrases.english: אביי said to him: If so,
say the latter clause:
if her fetus became noticeable in her womb,
she is ruined retroactively.
phrases.notes: The תרומה she already ate now turns out to have been forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: אִי הָכִי, אֵימָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's answer from step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that the first forty days are not affected by pregnancy.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says she is ruined retroactively, which seems to include the first forty days too.

steps.title: Retroactive only back to day forty
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers: 'ruined retroactively' only goes back to the fortieth day.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'ruined' mean? Back until forty days.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers אביי by explaining how far back 'retroactively' reaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The retroactive problem starts only from day forty of the pregnancy, when the fetus begins to count. What she ate in the first forty days stays permitted, so רב חסדא's answer holds.
steps.whatToRemember: A widowed בת כהן may eat תרומה for the first forty days. If a pregnancy later shows, only what she ate from day forty on was forbidden.

phrases.english: What is 'ruined'? Until forty days.
phrases.notes: Meaning the 'looking back' stops at day forty, so the first forty days stay permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מְקוּלְקֶלֶת — עַד אַרְבָּעִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge in step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining a word in the source ('ruined retroactively') more narrowly.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Retroactively' seemed to reach back to the very start of the pregnancy.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Retroactively' reaches back only to day forty, which fits רב חסדא's view.

steps.title: A child from relations with a betrothed woman: רב and שמואל disagree
steps.stepSummary: A new topic: a man had relations with his ארוסה in her father's house. רב says the child is a ממזר; שמואל says the child is a שתוקי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: one who had relations with his betrothed in his father-in-law's house: רב said the child is a ממזר, and שמואל said the child is a שתוקי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new discussion with a disagreement between רב and שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The woman is only betrothed and still lives in her father's house, so we cannot be sure the child is from her ארוס. רב treats the child as a ממזר, while שמואל treats him as a שתוקי, a child whose father is unknown.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated (an Amoraic disagreement follows)
A child born of a forbidden relationship
A child whose father is unknown

steps.confusionAlert: Relations between a man and his own ארוסה would not make a ממזר. רב's concern is that the child may really be from another man.

phrases.aramaic: אִיתְּמַר: הַבָּא עַל אֲרוּסָתוֹ בְּבֵית חָמִיו —
phrases.english: It was stated: one who had relations with his betrothed in his father-in-law's house,
רב said: the child is a ממזר,
and שמואל said: the child is a שתוקי.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: הַבָּא עַל אֲרוּסָתוֹ בְּבֵית חָמִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic, separate from the תרומה discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: the child is a ממזר. שמואל: the child is a שתוקי.

steps.title: רבא limits רב's view to a woman with a rumor about her
steps.stepSummary: רבא says רב's view makes sense only when she is rumored to be with other men. If there is no such rumor, we assume the child is from the ארוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: רב's statement makes sense when she is rumored to be with others. But if she is not rumored to be with others, we assume the child is his.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains when רב's ruling applies and narrows it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב calls the child a ממזר only when there is a rumor about the woman. Without a rumor, we assume the child belongs to the ארוס, who we know was with her.

keyTerms.meaning: She is rumored to be with other men

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, when there is no rumor about the woman, the child is assumed to be from the ארוס.

phrases.english: רבא said: רב's statement stands to reason
where she is rumored to be with others,
but if she is not rumored to be with others,
we cast the child after him.
phrases.notes: He means we assume the ארוס is the father.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מִסְתַּבְּרָא מִילְּתֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows רב's opinion from step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב's ruling applies only when there is a rumor about the woman. Otherwise, the child is assigned to the ארוס.

steps.title: רבא brings support from the משנה about a child of a כהן
steps.stepSummary: רבא points to a משנה: a woman who had relations with a כהן and gave birth may eat תרומה. This only makes sense if she was rumored with him alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Where do I get this from? The משנה teaches: if she gave birth, she may eat. What is the case? If she was rumored with other men, why should she eat just because she gave birth? So it must be that she was rumored only with him, and not with others.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא is starting to prove his claim from Step 25: if a woman is rumored only with one man, we assume the child is his. This is the first half of his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the child is treated as the כהן's child, so the mother may eat תרומה because of him. That would be impossible if she were rumored with other men too. So the משנה must be about a woman rumored only with the כהן, and still we assume the child is his.

keyTerms.meaning: Where do I get this from? (a request for a source)
She is rumored (to have been with someone)
What is the case? What are the circumstances?

phrases.english: Rava said: From where do I say it?
For it teaches: If she gave birth, she may eat.
phrases.notes: This is the משנה about a woman who was with a כהן without being married to him. Once she has his child, she may eat תרומה.

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If you say that she is rumored to be with others,
even if she gave birth, why may she eat?
Rather, is it not that she is rumored with him
and is not rumored with others?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source for רבא's statement in Step 25
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that when she is rumored only with one man, the child is assumed to be his
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה that a woman who gave birth from a כהן may eat תרומה

steps.title: The קל וחומר: if it works there, it surely works here
steps.stepSummary: רבא finishes his proof with a קל וחומר. In the משנה both men were forbidden to her, yet we assume the child is the כהן's. With an ארוסה, the ארוס is permitted, so we should surely assume the child is his.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there, where this man was forbidden to her and that man was forbidden to her, we still assume the child is his, then here, where that man was forbidden and this man (the ארוס) was permitted, is it not all the more so?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא takes the משנה from Step 26 and builds a קל וחומר from it to cover the case of the ארוסה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, being with the כהן and being with another man were both forbidden, and we still follow the man she was rumored with. With an ארוסה, being with her ארוס is permitted by the Torah, so the case for following him is even stronger. That is why רבא says רב's ruling of ממזר applies only when she is rumored with others.

keyTerms.meaning: We cast the child after him: we treat him as the father

steps.whyThisMatters: This קל וחומר is the heart of רבא's position. It is what אביי attacks next.

phrases.english: And if there,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the case in the משנה with the כהן.

phrases.english: where with this one it is forbidden and with that one it is forbidden,
we cast the child after him,
then here, where with that one it is forbidden
and with this one it is permitted,
is it not all the more so?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה הָתָם, דִּלְהַאי אִיסּוּרָא וּלְהַאי אִיסּוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the proof by applying the משנה to the ארוסה with a קל וחומר
steps.raayaObject: That the child of an ארוסה rumored only with her ארוס is his
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from the משנה about the כהן

steps.title: אביי rejects the proof
steps.stepSummary: אביי says רב rules ממזר even when she is rumored only with her ארוס. His reason is that a woman who was loose with her ארוס was probably loose with others too. He also explains that the משנה is about two people locked up alone in prison.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Really, I can tell you that whenever she is rumored with him, even if she is not rumored with others, רב said the child is a ממזר. Why? Because we say: since she was loose with her ארוס, she was loose with others too. And the משנה is talking about a case where the two of them were locked up in prison.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back against רבא's proof. He reads רב differently and explains away the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to אביי, an ארוסה who is with her ארוס before the wedding shows she is not careful, so we suspect other men too. The משנה is no proof, because there the woman and the כהן were locked up alone together, so no other man could be the father. This also breaks רבא's קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, I can tell you (used to reject a proof)
She made herself loose (was not careful about modesty)
A child born from a forbidden union

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying that being with an ארוס is forbidden like being with another man. His point is only that it shows she is careless, so we fear she was with others too.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Actually, I can say to you
that anywhere she is rumored with him,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא דָּיְימָא מֵעָלְמָא
phrases.english: even though she is not rumored with others,
Rav said the child is a mamzer.
What is the reason? Because we say:
since she made herself loose with the betrothed,
she made herself loose with others too.
And our mishna
is where the two of them were locked up in prison.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: לְעוֹלָם אֵימָא לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's proof and his reading of רב
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Both רבא's reading of רב and his proof from the משנה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה is a special case where the two were locked up alone, so no one else could be the father. With an ארוסה, being with her ארוס shows she is careless, so we suspect other men.
steps.whatToRemember: In the first version, אביי holds that רב calls the child a ממזר even when she is rumored only with her ארוס, because she showed she is careless.

steps.title: A second version of the argument between רב and שמואל
steps.stepSummary: Some say: if the ארוס admits he was with her, everyone agrees the child is his. The argument between רב and שמואל is only about a pregnant ארוסה. רב says the child is a ממזר, and שמואל says the child is a שתוקי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: when he was with her, everyone agrees we treat him as the father. The argument was said like this: about an ארוסה who became pregnant, רב says the child is a ממזר and שמואל says the child is a שתוקי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of the argument from Step 24. In this version, the case where the ארוס admits is not argued about at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, רב said ממזר even when the ארוס was the one with her. Here, when the ארוס admits, everyone agrees the child is his. The argument is moved to a pregnant ארוסה whose ארוס does not admit being with her.

keyTerms.meaning: A betrothed woman who became pregnant
A child whose father is unknown

phrases.english: Some say:
When he had relations with her,
phrases.notes: This means the ארוס admits that he was with her.

phrases.english: everyone agrees
that we cast the child after him.
And this is how it was stated:
A betrothed woman who became pregnant,
Rav said: The child is a mamzer.
And Shmuel said: The child is a shetuki.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: בְּבָא עָלֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the argument from Step 24, changing the case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the ארוס admits, the child is his according to everyone. With a pregnant ארוסה, רב says ממזר and שמואל says שתוקי.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions. In this version, the ממזר ruling does not apply when the ארוס admits he was with her.

steps.title: רבא explains when רב's view makes sense in the second version
steps.stepSummary: רבא says רב's ruling of ממזר makes sense where she is not rumored with her ארוס but is rumored with other men.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: רב's statement makes sense where she is not rumored with him, and she is rumored with others.
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the second version, רבא limits רב's ruling to a specific case. His sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she was never linked to her ארוס but was linked to other men, it is reasonable to assume the child came from another man. That is why רב calls the child a ממזר in that case.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense, it is reasonable

phrases.english: Rava said: Rav's statement makes sense
where she is not rumored with him
and she is rumored with others,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מִסְתַּבְּרָא מִילְּתֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רב's ruling within the second version
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב's ruling of ממזר is reasonable when she is rumored with others and not with her ארוס.
